g_rules.text: Single post: hook first, plus exactly 2 alternative hooks
Single post skips brief, units table and calendar (unless a source asset)
Voice source order: account card, else brand card, else fallback order; label 'voice provisional'
Never open voice interview for one post; offer to build a voice card afterwards
Every piece carries an edit note
Every piece carries a claims check: kept, softened, cut, and what would restore each cut
Handover order: title and path; piece; edit note; claims check; open gaps
Open gaps tagged [PROOF NEEDED: ...], [CUSTOMER APPROVAL NEEDED], [NAME: ...], PERSON YES NEEDED
Fixed closing line: Nothing is published, you edit and post; offer two-week posting calendar, ask for it next
Claims sign-off basis stated: signed-off <date> | scoped sign-off this run | product facts only
Opinions, stories, first-person experience only from the human/named person; never write unsupplied 'we believe/I've learned'; leave [NAME: your take] slots
Anything published under or quoting a named person carries PERSON YES NEEDED (<name>)
Sponsored/affiliate/gifted/collab piece: apply disclosure rules
Claims block format: 'Claims and facts <piece> (sign-off: ...)' then Kept, Softened, Cut (restore), Sourced (url, date opened), Disclaimers added, Person yes needed: <name>|none
World fact needs a public source opened this run, cited inline with date; else cut or make it a plain instruction; never from memory
Competitor fact dated and sourced
Quote only with link to its page; else paraphrase without quote marks or cut
Price/plan/offer checked live; saved price is a lead, not copy
Limitation about us only from product record or human; never inferred
Sensitive topic: resource line or [RESOURCE LINE NEEDED]; no product tie-in; drop dated framing
Third-party IP or real person's name/likeness only with confirmed permission; else generic
Brand's own past posts and site copy are voice examples, not proof
Show cuts in plain words; never name internal steps, tools or playbooks
LinkedIn on a person's profile: first person, story or earned lesson, only from their own words
LinkedIn on a company page: 'we' voice, no first-person story
First ~2 lines (~140 to 210 chars before 'see more') must make someone expand
Short paragraphs, but not one sentence per line throughout
LinkedIn post 900 to 1,800 characters
Link goes in first comment, or is dropped; never in body
0 to 3 hashtags
Length follows intent; never pad
Edit note carries One argument, Swap test, Fakes, Intent and CTA (substance Q1, 3, 8, 9)
One argument: a disagreeable one-sentence thesis; every section advances it; cut unneeded sections
'So what?' after each paragraph; rewrite or cut
Swap test: if it works with a competitor's name, add own data/opinion or say it is generic
Information gain judged only against competitor content in hand; else 'not checked'
Skeptic: answer the strongest objection in the piece
Order: strongest point early
Fakes: remove unsupplied anecdotes, customers, stats; replace with [PROOF NEEDED]/[STORY NEEDED] or cut; every proof unit traces to the brief
CTA matches intent; no demo ask on learn piece; offer next useful step
Hedge once where genuinely uncertain; no stacked hedges; take a verdict
Hook promises what is delivered in first 100 words; leads with reader's pain/want, never own weakness or rival comparison
Lede: claim or tension by sentence two; no scene-setting; no 'In today's'
Paragraphs <=4 lines, one idea each; bold at most once per section; lists only for parallel items
Sentences average <=18 words with variation; grade 7 to 9 B2B (a check)
Ending: no recap; end on implication, next action or held-back line
Voice match against 3 example lines via fallback order; apply voice-guide Do/Don'ts and learnings; remove guessed humour
AI-tell banned word list (delve, unlock, leverage, journey, game-changer, ...)
AI-tell banned phrase list (In today's, Moreover, Here's the kicker, Let that sink in, Ready to...?, ...)
'Not X, it's Y' / 'not just X but Y' at most once per piece
No rhetorical-question openers
No self-answered questions ('Why? Because...')
No colon reveals ('The result? ...')
No triplet adjective lists or three parallel clauses in a row
Em dashes rare, at brand's own rate
Not every paragraph the same length
Not every section ends in a summary sentence
No bolded phrases scattered through every paragraph
No invented dialogue in quote marks
No Title Case hooks on social
A tell is allowed if the brand's own real writing uses it
Report removed tells with counts in the notes ('removed: 3 x leverage, 2 x colon reveals')
